newsitem.title: UK: Firm dollar pushes Euro bourses to records.
newsitem.headline: Firm dollar pushes Euro bourses to records.

text.p: The dollar held firm against the mark on Tuesday as traders saw uncertainties in China and the Middle East as new reasons to buy the U.S. currency, propelling continental European stock markets to record levels.
In Paris and Frankfurt the dollar's strength, which helps European exporters, snuffed out Monday's modest profit-taking and pushed shares to record levels.

But British investors, who have no weak currency to help local exporters, were less enthusiastic. While the London share market was modestly higher, investors awaited guidance from Wall Street after a long weekend in the United States.
For once, currency dealers spoke less about interest rates and more about two fresh factors, the health of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping and trouble in the Middle East.

News that top Chinese officials were hurriedly returning to Beijing from trips outside the capital shook Asian stock markets as investors feared that the 93-year-old Deng, who led China's economic reforms, might die soon.
The Chinese Foreign Ministry said there had been no major change in Deng's health. But dealers said the possibility of Chinese instability was a reason to buy dollars.

The Middle East weighed in, with Tehran Radio reporting that Iranian security forces had clashed with members of an Iraq-based opposition group, killing three and wounding another. But Iraq denied reports that it was massing troops near its border with Kuwait.
The dollar climbed to 1.7028 marks at late morning from 1.6997 at Monday's European close but eased to 124.18 yen from Monday's 124.50.

Dealers said the buying against the mark reflected jittery markets wondering whether central banks would intervene to slow the dollar's rise. This follows a recent meeting of finance ministers and central bank governors from the Group of Seven leading industrial nations.

"Since G7 all the talk seems to have been about central bank intervention even though it wasn't even discussed at the meeting," said one trader. "This is making people nervous but when an excuse comes along to buy dollars they grab it with both hands."

While interest rates slipped from the top of traders' concerns, worries are growing before U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan gives his Humphrey Hawkins testimony to Congress on February 27.

Away from the dollar, the lira skidded amid concern that Italy might not make the first wave of European economic and monetary union (EMU). The lira was at 988.80 to the mark, compared with 987.25 late on Monday.

Dealers blamed comments from Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi and Belgian central bank chief Alfonse Verplaetse. Prodi said on Monday that Germany was less committed to EMU than Italy, fuelling rumours that Bonn was conspiring to keep the lira out of the first wave of nations joining the European currency's launch.
Verplaetse also made comments apparently questioning the lira's suitability for early EMU entry, although he later denied he had been referring to Italy.
On equity markets, London's FTSE 100 index was up 9.9 points at 4,347.7 points but failed to hit last Friday's record high of 4,353.4, unlike its continental counterparts.
"We had no lead from Wall Street today so it's very much a stock-by-stock and sector-by-sector situation," a dealer said.

One uncertainty disappeared, for the time being at least, when the Conservative government survived a parliamentary censure motion on Monday night which could have led to a confidence vote and an early election.
Germany's DAX index was up 46.76 points, or 1.45 percent, at 3,279.33, while France's CAC-40 index gained 21.90. or 0.83 percent, to 2,656.38.

"The dollar is still the engine for the gains," said one Frankfurt dealer. Good bank results also helped to push up prices, although traders said the market still needed a consolidation after this year's heady gains.
CURRENCIES AT 1130 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7028 marks and 124.18 yen compared with 1.6997 marks and 124.50 yen in late European trading on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1130 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 9.9 points at 4,347.7.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 21.90 at 2,656.38 points.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was 46.76 points higher at 3,279.33.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1130 GMT
Gold rose to $346.25 an ounce from the morning fixing of $346.00 and Monday's closing at $344.25. Silver was up four cents at $5.25.
